races.name: Winning Experience With Moulton Racing Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Pierian
runners_data.note: Front running style perfectly suits small field dynamics, excellent recent form progression, and Marquand/Haggas team firing
runners_data.spotlight: Dam 1m2f-1m4f winner (including Irish Oaks); made a promising start when a close second at Wetherby (1m2f, good to firm) last month and she built on that when finishing well to win at Salisbury (1m2f, good) two weeks ago; looks a useful prospect and she has lots in hand on the figures over her sole rival.

runners_data.name: Spirit Dreamer
runners_data.note: Hold-up style needs strong pace to be effective, struggling recent form suggests outclassed, Watson needs to time run perfectly
runners_data.spotlight: Closely related to a 1m4f AW winner but he's struggled at biggish prices at Salisbury (1m4f, good to firm) and Haydock (11.6f, soft) this month; still early days but this is a daunting task and handicaps will be more suitable.

races.paceDynamic: Pierian will take the lead from the start with no other confirmed front runners in this small field. Spirit Dreamer's hold-up style means he'll sit behind the pace and wait for his chance. With only two runners, Pierian can dictate a comfortable tempo without pressure, potentially stretching clear in the straight. This race shape strongly favours the front runner who can control the gallop and kick when ready.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pierian Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Pierian breaks cleanly and settles into rhythm
scenarios.body: She can dictate her own fractions and has the class edge to resist any late challenge. Her prominent style perfectly suits having a clear lead with no early pressure.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Spirit Dreamer Late Rally
scenarios.trigger: If Pierian goes too fast early or Spirit Dreamer gets perfect run
scenarios.body: The hold-up horse could benefit from a strong pace and time his run perfectly. Watson would need to produce Spirit Dreamer with a perfectly-timed challenge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Finish
scenarios.trigger: If both horses go too conservatively early
scenarios.body: A tactical affair could turn into a sprint finish where either could prevail. The race would become more about who has the better turn of foot in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Early Tactical Battle
scenarios.trigger: If Spirit Dreamer tries to make running unexpectedly
scenarios.body: This would completely change the race dynamic but seems highly unlikely given his hold-up style. It would create an unnatural pace scenario for both.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Pierian breaks slowly or gets shuffled back early as her whole tactical advantage depends on taking the lead
Watch Spirit Dreamer's position turning for home - if he's too far back he won't have time to make up ground
Watch the early fractions - if Pierian goes too fast she could set it up for Spirit Dreamer's late kick

races.name: Download The At The Races App Handicap

runners_data.name: Fifty Nifty
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning after 157 days off with solid course form but faces fitness concerns
runners_data.spotlight: Dual fast-ground winner (1m/7f) for Tom Clover, including on his debut at this track in April 2024; shaped quite well at Kempton (6f, AW) in December but failed to build on that next time and has since left Mick Appleby; has bit to prove after six months off but he's had wind surgery and needs watching in market on stable debut.

runners_data.name: Zubaru
runners_data.note: Progressive hold-up type in excellent current form with two recent wins, ideally suited to tactical finish
runners_data.spotlight: Progressive 4yo who made the breakthrough when forging clear at Doncaster (7f, good to firm) and he followed up under a penalty at Leicester 19 days ago; up another 4lb but he's on a roll and is still relatively lightly raced; big player.

runners_data.name: Berry Clever
runners_data.note: Just won over course and distance but up in grade under penalty, consistent hold-up performer
runners_data.spotlight: Added to his three AW wins when justifying favouritism over C&D (good) last week; goes back up in grade under a penalty but he was as good as ever last time and he's effective on good to firm; shortlisted.

runners_data.name: Dapper Guest
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse struggling this season despite last year's success, needs to rediscover best form
runners_data.spotlight: Defied this mark at Chelmsford (7f, AW) last October but he's been out of sorts at Newmarket and Ascot in his two runs this season; now drops back in grade but he's 1-13 on turf and others are more convincing; reapplied visor replaces cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Jakarta
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner returning after 224 days off with juvenile promise but fitness questions remain
runners_data.spotlight: Dual winning juvenile (maiden/nursery) who was off for 324 days before showing mixed form in three starts from September last year, just failing in Newmarket handicap (1m, good) but lesser shows either side of that; it's encouraging that this year's campaign is starting earlier but she comes with risks attached after eight months off; tongue-tie added.

runners_data.name: Stenmark
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse switching trainers after three-month break, solid AW form but turf effectiveness unclear
runners_data.spotlight: Won at Southwell (7f, Tapeta) last summer and he posted three solid efforts on AW during the winter; returns for new trainer after three months off but he's effective on turf and seems versatile ground-wise in this sphere; dangerous in first-time cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Daring Legend
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer struggling on turf this year despite AW promise, needs significant improvement
runners_data.spotlight: Reappeared for new yard with a near-miss at Kempton (6f, AW) in March but he's struggled at 50-1 back on turf in last two runs; got hampered early on at Ascot last time but he's hard to predict and needs to bounce back near best.

runners_data.name: Drifts Away
runners_data.note: Key pace angle as the lone front runner returning after nine months off, won this race last year
runners_data.spotlight: Big improver in the first half of last year, with four wins and latest was in this race; struggled in final two runs last season but he remains feasibly treated on his best form and is still lightly raced on turf; needs a close look back from 273 days off.

runners_data.name: Sea Suite
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in consistent form with recent Tapeta success, likely to track the leader throughout
runners_data.spotlight: Record of 1-12 but his win came at Southwell (7f, Tapeta) in March and he's held his form with three creditable efforts since; still looks on a workable mark and he's respected in suitable conditions back on turf.

races.paceDynamic: Drifts Away represents the sole confirmed front runner and will likely dictate terms from the start, with Sea Suite possibly tracking in second. With most runners preferring hold-up tactics, the early pace should be sustainable rather than punishing, allowing Drifts Away to control fractions through the first half-mile. The lack of early pace pressure means the race will likely develop into a tactical affair where positioning matters more than raw speed. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners who can sit close to the pace and hold-up horses with a proven finishing kick.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sustainable pace holds
scenarios.trigger: If Drifts Away sets modest fractions and isn't pressured early
scenarios.body: The steady tempo allows closers time to organize while prominent runners maintain ideal positioning throughout. Hold-up horses with proven finishing speed can unleash their kicks in the final two furlongs without facing an impossible task.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front runner dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Drifts Away finds his rhythm and kicks clear turning for home
scenarios.body: The lack of early pressure allows the leader to conserve energy before accelerating when it matters. Prominent runners tracking closely get first run on the rest but struggle to match the leader's sustained drive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical sprint finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely in the middle stages
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure speed test over the final three furlongs where class and finishing kick matter most. Only horses with genuine tactical pace can position themselves for the final surge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace collapse suits outsider
scenarios.trigger: If positioning becomes chaotic and favorites get trapped
scenarios.body: The stop-start nature of the race plays into the hands of an unfancied runner who finds clear running at the right moment. Patient jockeyship becomes more valuable than pure ability.

watchPoints.text: Drifts Away's fitness after 273 days off - if he weakens late the race opens up dramatically for closers
Berry Clever carrying penalty after last week's win - watch if the extra weight tells in the closing stages
Jakarta and Fifty Nifty both returning after lengthy breaks - monitor early positioning for signs of ring-rustiness
Sea Suite's positioning behind Drifts Away - if he gets too close too early he may not have finishing kick left
Zubaru's ability to secure clear running room given his hold-up style in a race likely to develop late

races.name: British Stallion Studs EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Bincimbal
runners_data.spotlight: Late-March first foal by Too Darn Hot; 325,000gns yearling; dam 7f 2yo winner (RPR 99), closely related to 1m Group 3 winner Komorebi, half-sister to winners Bright Melody (Group-placed 1m1f/1m2f) and Hawk Power (Listed-placed 1m2f), out of Group 1 Fillies' Mile winner; first juvenile runner of the year for his stable and sales price/pedigree demand a market check.

runners_data.name: Byzantine
runners_data.spotlight: St Mark's Basilica May (seventh) foal; 65,000euros yearling, 86,000euros breeze-up 2yo; half-brother to winners Open Secret (1m6f Flat, RPR 81; 2m3f hurdle) and Lone Fighter (7f AW; 72); dam 7.6f 2yo winner (98), half-sister to a useful 1m-1m6f Flat and 2m/2m5f hurdle winner; foaling date and mixed pedigree muddy the water but yard is off the mark with this year's 2yos and the betting should provide plenty of clues.

runners_data.name: Eagle Island
runners_data.spotlight: By Camelot; January (ninth) foal; 150,000gns yearling; half-brother to winners Martlet (1m2f-1m4f including Listed; RPR 110), Stowell (Group-placed 1m4f; 109), Keswick (9.4f/1m2f AW; 87) and Palmerston (1m/8.4f; 86); dam 1m3f winner (90), out of Irish Oaks winner; yard had its first 2yo winner of the year fairly recently; market check essential.

runners_data.name: Shiyam
runners_data.spotlight: March (fifth) foal; 200,000gns yearling; half-brother to winners Luther (7f/1m including 2yo Listed/US Grade 2; RPR 115), Good Gracious (Listed-placed 7f AW 2yo/1m turf; 101) and Offer And Receive (1m 2yo/Swedish 7f; 79); dam 7.6f 2yo/1m2f Group 3 winner (101); many an eye will be trained on this first representative as a sire for brilliant racehorse Baaeed so fascinating to see how he goes in the market before showing what he can do.

runners_data.name: Al Hudaiba
runners_data.spotlight: 5-1 and he stabilised a yard wobble when looking green but still coming out on top in six-runner Newmarket novice (6f, good) on his debut a fortnight ago; that form is yet to be tested but the runner-up topped an April breeze-up sale at £880,000 so it will be disappointing if it doesn't work out; the one to aim at under his penalty.

races.name: Norwich Inns Handicap

runners_data.name: Hengest
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with excellent recent form including two wins, but faces tactical disadvantage against confirmed front runner
runners_data.spotlight: Lightly raced 4yo; won in good style on handicap debut at Windsor (1m2f, good to firm) 17 days ago and he followed up with an odds-on win at Lingfield (11.6f, good) last week; only 4lb higher under a penalty here and he's open to more progress in middle-distance handicaps; big player.

runners_data.name: Give Me The Night
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who benefits from 10lb drop in weights and proximity to likely pace setter, though remains a maiden after eight attempts
runners_data.spotlight: Eight-race maiden who has not lived up to his initial promise and he's been well held in five handicaps (7f/1m); now 10lb lower than for his opening mark but he needs a transformation at this new trip.

runners_data.name: Man Of Desert
runners_data.note: Another hold-up horse and ten-race maiden with traffic issues last time, faces difficulty getting competitive position from the back
runners_data.spotlight: Ten-race maiden who has form figures of 0487057 in handicaps; had some traffic issues when prominent in the market at Kempton last week but this is competitive back on turf and he still has stamina to prove at this trip; others preferred.

runners_data.name: King's Hand
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with good recent form for new trainer but needs pace to aim at, which may not materialise here
runners_data.spotlight: Polytrack winner for Sir Mark Prescott in January; two good runs to start off his time with Joseph Parr and he took a step forward when seeing off seven rivals at Lingfield (1m2f, good) ten days ago; this is tougher under a penalty but he did well to overcome a slow start last time and he's still unexposed on turf; respected.

runners_data.name: Harlington
runners_data.note: Only confirmed front runner with proven stamina gets tactical advantage, though 38 days since last run adds slight fitness question
runners_data.spotlight: Six time winner who won three in a row in January/February and he ran another good race when third at Lingfield (1m2f, Polytrack) last month; won on turf last summer but that was off a much lower mark and he needs to transfer his progress back to this sphere.

races.paceDynamic: Harlington is the only confirmed front runner in this small field and should get an uncontested lead with Give Me The Night sitting prominent behind. The lack of pace pressure means Harlington can dictate terms and kick for home when ready, while the three hold-up horses (Hengest, Man Of Desert, King's Hand) will need to time their runs perfectly from the back. This sustainable pace scenario strongly favours front runners and prominent racers who can stay close to the action throughout.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Front Runner Dominance
scenarios.trigger: If Harlington gets soft fractions and kicks clear turning for home
scenarios.body: The lack of pace pressure allows the front runner to control the race completely, making it difficult for hold-up horses to make up ground in time. Harlington's proven stamina and tactical advantage become decisive factors.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge From Class
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is steady enough for Hengest to produce his finishing kick
scenarios.body: The improving 4-year-old times his run to perfection and his superior recent form tells, despite giving away a tactical advantage to the pace setters. His two recent wins show he's peaking at the right time.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Give Me The Night travels well in second and finds improvement off his lowered mark
scenarios.body: The maiden gets the perfect trip behind Harlington and finally breaks through when the pace quickens, benefiting from the tactical position without the pressure of making the running. His 10lb drop in the weights proves crucial.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Coordination
scenarios.trigger: If multiple hold-up horses combine to pressure the leaders late
scenarios.body: King's Hand and Man Of Desert work together to apply late pressure, but this requires perfect timing and strong pace to be effective. The numbers game works against the front runners despite their tactical advantage.

watchPoints.text: Harlington gets uncontested lead and dictates fractions - could prove impossible to peg back with tactical advantage
Give Me The Night travels prominently behind Harlington - best positioned maiden to finally break through off reduced mark
Hengest needs strong pace to be effective but may struggle to make up ground if Harlington controls tempo
King's Hand and Man Of Desert both need to overcome hold-up disadvantage in small field lacking genuine pace
Tom Marquand's positioning of Man Of Desert in early stages will indicate connections' confidence in his chances

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Virgin 512 Handicap

runners_data.name: First Folio
runners_data.note: Excellent Yarmouth record with three wins from five starts here, prominent style suits the likely tempo
runners_data.spotlight: Five visits here have resulted in three wins and two places, all at 6f; made an encouraging return when fourth of nine at Ripon three weeks ago and he's slipped to a dangerous mark; tempting.

runners_data.name: Fantasy Master
runners_data.note: Sharp early speed for Robert Cowell, won here in December and showed that gate pace at Ascot last time
runners_data.spotlight: Wasted little time getting off the mark for this yard when scoring at Chelmsford (AW) in December and it was a fine return when flying out of the stalls before finishing third of 18 at Ascot (again 6f, good to firm; Neyva's Angel fourth) 19 days ago; said to look "absolutely superb" in a recent stable tour and he's a must for the shortlist off the same mark.

runners_data.name: Carbine Harvester
runners_data.note: Prominent racer from powerful Haggas yard but wind operation suggests breathing issues may persist
runners_data.spotlight: Ended 2025 with two good AW runs at Kempton; down the field in three AW starts this year and he had been given a wind op before weakening on his return to turf at Windsor (6f, good to firm) 17 days ago; nothing wrong with this mark and he drops in grade but the jury's out at the moment.

runners_data.name: Valley Ofthe Kings
runners_data.spotlight: Two AW wins last year include one at 6f; didn't run at all badly when midfield in a stronger handicap than this at Doncaster (6f, good to soft) in March but he finished last of nine at Catterick the following month; connections blamed the undulations that day and he'll have no such concerns this time.

runners_data.name: Twilight Fun
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner who should get soft lead, but his recent 5f flop raises stamina questions back at 6f
runners_data.spotlight: Tends to lead; started the year well on AW but it all went wrong at Newcastle in March and he could only beat one home in seven-runner 5f course handicap a fortnight ago; easy ground probably no help that day and it's not impossible this C&D winner can stage a revival.

runners_data.name: Another Abbot
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with strong 6f record on sound surfaces, needs luck from back but has class edge
runners_data.spotlight: Beaten just over 2l when an encouraging seventh of 17 at Ascot (5f, good to firm) at the start of the month; both of last year's wins came at 6f on a sound surface so has conditions to suit and he's a candidate to step forward.

runners_data.name: Neyva's Angel
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who won well last time but traffic problems likely from rear in compact field
runners_data.spotlight: Broke her duck in a Southwell handicap last month then bungled the start before seeing little daylight when fourth of 18 at Ascot (6f, good to firm; Fantasy Master third) 19 days ago; looked to finish that event with a fair bit more to give and she's a key player.

runners_data.name: Style King
runners_data.note: Prominent runner carrying bottom weight but winless on turf in five attempts for this yard
runners_data.spotlight: 0-5 on turf; didn't build on his second at Wolverhampton in April when favourite but flopping at Southwell (also 6f, AW) a fortnight later; others hold more pressing claims.

runners_data.name: Travel Agent
runners_data.note: In-form hold-up runner with two recent wins, eyeshield helping but needs gaps to appear
runners_data.spotlight: Quickly clicked into gear for this yard with an eyeshield fitted, scoring twice on AW in April before close second at Lingfield (also 6f, good) last Monday; due for a 1lb nudge in future and he can't be ignored.

runners_data.name: Izzy Fast
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare whose 50-1 maiden win was impressive but 18-length handicap debut suggests this is harder
runners_data.spotlight: Made a proper splash when going in at 50-1 on her reappearance in C&D maiden (good; third start) in April but contrasting fortunes when beaten 18l on her handicap debut at Newmarket 12 days ago; that was too bad to be true but does lower expectations somewhat.

races.paceDynamic: Twilight Fun is the only confirmed early leader and should get an uncontested lead through steady fractions in this 6f handicap. Behind him, First Folio, Fantasy Master, Carbine Harvester and Valley Of The Kings will create a bunched prominent group, setting up potential traffic problems turning for home. With three hold-up horses (Another Abbot, Neyva's Angel, Travel Agent, Izzy Fast) needing late room in a compact 10-runner field, the lack of early pace pressure should allow prominent runners to outkick the closers. This race shape clearly favours front-runners and prominent racers who can secure clear racing room.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Twilight Fun gets soft fractions and isn't headed approaching the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The moderate early pace allows him to conserve energy before kicking clear, while the prominent pack behind struggle to reel him back in time. His front-running style becomes a major asset rather than a liability.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent quartet get first run on Twilight Fun turning for home.
scenarios.body: Fantasy Master and First Folio can utilize their tactical speed to sweep past the tiring leader, while the hold-up horses get caught in traffic behind the prominent wall. The early positioning proves decisive in a sprint finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners go too hard chasing down Twilight Fun in the final 2f.
scenarios.body: Travel Agent or Another Abbot find the gaps as the early leaders tie up, benefiting from the honest pace and their fresh finish. Their class tells when others have shot their bolt.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Sprint
scenarios.trigger: If Twilight Fun stops badly and the prominent pack also falter from the sustained effort.
scenarios.body: The race becomes a mad dash where any horse with a turn of foot can win, favoring those who conserved most energy. Positioning becomes irrelevant in a blanket finish.

watchPoints.text: Travel Agent and Another Abbot could get boxed in behind the wall of four prominent runners if they don't get early cover
Twilight Fun's stamina must be questioned after his poor 5f effort last time when failing to see out the trip
Fantasy Master showed sharp early pace at Ascot and could press Twilight Fun harder than expected if bouncing out fast
First Folio has won three times at this course and track conditions are ideal for another bold showing
The prominent quartet of First Folio, Fantasy Master, Carbine Harvester and Valley Of The Kings could create a moving wall that blocks the closers

races.name: Get Raceday Ready Handicap

runners_data.name: Merapi
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with strong recent course form who should benefit from the likely strong pace and handles good ground well
runners_data.spotlight: 0-14 but she finished runner-up twice here (1m/1m1f) last month and had another close call at Wolverhampton two weeks ago; on same mark as for her last two runs and she should make another bold bid; cheekpieces added.

runners_data.name: Siam Fox
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning to course and distance of his last win but struggling for form despite wind surgery
runners_data.spotlight: C&D winner but his last success was almost two years ago; very well treated on old form but he's struggled in last five starts including after wind surgery here (1m good; 22-1) two weeks ago; blinkers are now tried and cheekpieces are removed.

runners_data.name: King Of Charm
runners_data.note: Hold-up type on a long absence whose mark has dropped significantly but needs major form turnaround
runners_data.spotlight: Thrown in on his 3yo form but 2025 was disappointing and he's struggled in both runs this year; mark continues to fall but he needs a needs a big turnaround in first-time cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: El Fox
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with consistent recent efforts who should appreciate the likely strong gallop from her prominent position
runners_data.spotlight: 0-9 but she's reached the frame in four of her handicaps including when fourth on C&D reappearance (good) two weeks ago; that was behind a major improver and she's a player if he can build on that.

runners_data.name: Charlatan
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer returning to turf after mixed AW form, could benefit from sustained pace but long absence concerning
runners_data.spotlight: Gained his fifth AW success when winning at Wolverhampton (8.6f) in December; mixed results in four subsequent runs but he rallied for fourth at Southwell (7f, AW) in March; now returns to turf but he has placed form in this sphere and is not ruled out back up in trip.

runners_data.name: Typeface
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with turf wins who disappointed last time despite market support, needs to recapture best form
runners_data.spotlight: Dual turf winner but has mixed record since his emphatic win at Ffos Las (1m, good) last August; didn't live up to market expectations on Doncaster reappearance (good to soft) 12 days ago but he missed the break and may have needed that run; should be sharper this time and has possibilities if he can rediscover his spark.

runners_data.name: Suitcase Smith
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has struggled to get competitive recently and looks outclassed despite handicapper's help
runners_data.spotlight: Unexposed 4yo but he's not finished closer than 6l to a winner and was a remote seventh over C&D (good) two weeks ago; dropped another 3lb but he's hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Kitty's Dream
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer returning after 234-day break with tendency to fade in finish, major question marks
runners_data.spotlight: Struggled in six runs for Alice Haynes including three handicaps (7f-8.6f); returns for new yard after 234 days off and she has a lot to prove; equipment removed.

runners_data.name: Regal Guest
runners_data.note: Only confirmed leader whose tactical advantage is significant but form figures suggest he needs career-best effort
runners_data.spotlight: Promising third at Kempton (7f, AW) last March on his second start but has beaten only one rival in three handicaps since; still lightly raced but he needs a transformation at this new trip; cheekpieces added.

races.paceDynamic: Regal Guest is the only confirmed front runner in this field of mainly hold-up performers, giving him a clear tactical advantage to dictate terms without early pressure. With eight hold-up horses behind him, the pace is likely to be steady early before quickening from the 3f pole as the field bunches up. The sustained gallop on good to firm ground will test stamina reserves, while the lone leader gets first run on his rivals. This race shape strongly favours the early leader and any prominent racers who can track the pace, as the hold-up brigade will face a wall of horses when making their moves.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Regal Guest breaks cleanly and isn't pressed early
scenarios.body: He can dictate a comfortable gallop and kick clear when the field closes, while the mass of hold-up horses get in each other's way. The tactical advantage of being alone on the lead proves decisive on this course configuration.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Benefits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Regal Guest goes too slow early or gets headed
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where the hold-up horses can unleash their finishing kicks together. Superior class and recent form become the deciding factors in a bunched finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Regal Guest Folds Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early leader sets too strong a gallop or ties up
scenarios.body: His effort becomes unsustainable in the final furlong, allowing the best staying hold-up horse to sweep past. The pace scenario still suits those who raced prominently rather than from the back.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise Pace Rival Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If one of the hold-up horses breaks character and races keenly
scenarios.body: This creates genuine pace pressure on Regal Guest and changes the entire complexion to a more even gallop. The race opens up for horses with tactical speed who can position prominently.

watchPoints.text: Regal Guest's early fractions - if he goes too fast trying to build a lead, he'll tie up badly in the straight
Any hold-up horse that breaks character and races keenly early will completely change the pace dynamic
Merapi's position turning in - her recent course form suggests she's the main danger if getting a clear run
The inside rail for traffic problems - with eight hold-up horses, congestion is likely in the straight
Charlatan's turf readiness after 78-day break - his class could tell if finding his best form first time back
